title: Mandala — five rounds
subtitle: A 20 cm flat-circle mandala — flat-circle base for four rounds, decorative shell edging on round 5
excerpt: Five rounds expand the three-round mandala base with two more flat-circle double-crochet rounds before a final shell edging. At 20 cm diameter in DK cotton on a 4 mm hook, the five-round mandala is the standard bag-base size and a confident standalone wall piece or centrepiece.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), circular motif chapter. Weldon's Practical Crochet — the doily and round-mat construction.
heroPrompt: A five-round crochet mandala in two colours — a warm terracotta centre and cream outer round — on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. The 20 cm flat circle shows four rounds of double crochet and an outer shell edging with six radiating petal groups.

chartDefinition.caption: Five rounds from the magic ring. Rounds 1 to 4 work flat-circle double crochet with six increases per round. Round 5 is a shell edging of treble groups separated by chain-2 spaces.

glossaryTerms.definition: A circle that lies flat without cupping or ruffling. In crochet, a flat circle in double crochet requires six increases per round — one at each of six evenly-spaced points. More increases per round causes ruffling; fewer causes cupping.

Multiple trebles worked into the same stitch or space, fanning outward to create a shell or petal shape. In the five-round mandala, a shell of five trebles sits at each of the six radiating points on round 5.

content.text: The five-round mandala takes the three-round version's
flat-circle
base and extends it two more rounds before the decorative
shell

edging. Four double-crochet rounds (six increases per round, distributed evenly) build a solid 18 cm circle before round 5 replaces the increase pattern with six five-treble shell groups separated by chain-2 spaces. The finished diameter is 20 cm after steam-blocking.

Round 5 is the first round that carries a distinct colour contrast in multi-colour versions — a different colour for the shell round sets the mandala's radiating structure clearly visible without needing to count rounds. For a single-colour version, the shell round still reads as a distinct petal ring against the tighter double-crochet background.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 15 g of DK-weight cotton in one to two colours. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Gauge

Each finished five-round mandala measures 20 cm diameter in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a light steam-block. Make a three-round test motif first and check it measures 14 cm — that confirms your tension is correct before continuing to rounds 4 and 5.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; called single crochet (sc) in US patterns.
treble (tr) — UK; called double crochet (dc) in US patterns.
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Place a stitch marker in the first stitch of each double-crochet round to track the round boundary. Do not turn.
Round 1
Form a magic ring. Ch 1. Work 6 dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc to join. Pull tail to close ring. (6 dc.)
Round 2
Ch 1. Work 2 dc into each stitch around. Sl st to first dc to join. (12 dc.)
Round 3
Ch 1. *2 dc in next st, 1 dc in next st*; repeat from * to * five more times. Sl st to first dc to join. (18 dc.)
Round 4
Ch 1. *2 dc in next st, 1 dc in each of next 2 sts*; repeat from * to * five more times. Sl st to first dc to join. (24 dc.)
Round 5 — Shell edging

If changing colour, fasten off round 4 yarn and join new colour. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Into same stitch work 4 tr. *Ch 2, skip 3 sts, 5 tr into next st*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (6 shells of 5 tr, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Chart
The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Rounds 1 to 4 show flat-circle double crochet with six evenly-distributed increases per round. Round 5 shows the six five-treble shell groups.

definition.title: Mandala — five rounds
definition.caption: Five rounds from the magic ring. Rounds 1 to 4: flat-circle double crochet with six increases per round. Round 5: six shell groups of 5 tr each separated by ch-2 spaces.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Weave through 3 to 4 stitches on the wrong side of round 5, reverse direction through 2 to 3 stitches, and trim. Weave in the magic ring tail and any colour-change tails. Steam-block on a blocking mat — pin each of the six shell groups and ease the circle into a true circle with a pin at every chain-2 space.
Joining

The five-round mandala works best as a standalone motif — a bag base, a wall piece, or a pot holder. For a blanket or panel, join through the chain-2 spaces of adjacent shell rounds with a flat slip-stitch seam on the wrong side, and fill the gaps between circles with small treble triangles or a surface-crochet grid.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap, or machine-wash on a delicates cycle. Lay flat to dry on a clean towel and ease the circle back into shape while damp.
What to try next

The eight-round mandala extends to 30 cm diameter and introduces V-stitches and a picot edging in the later rounds. The lacy mandala replaces the solid double-crochet base with open double-treble fans from round 3, giving a much airier version of the same radiating structure.
